macro.headline: Hawkish Fed, energy & geopolitics in the driver's seat
macro.body: Fed Chair Warsh scrapped forward guidance and the dot plot leans toward hikes, not cuts, so long-duration high-multiple growth (NOW, ADBE, NVDA, IOT) stays rate-sensitive. Energy and the Strait of Hormuz headlines are the live swing factor on inflation.

risk.detail: FY guide cut (Jun 4): Americas comps −5% (5th straight), tariffs gutted margins, China stalled.
FY26 growth cut 10.5→7–8.5%; Watchman/EP/urology soft; mgmt guides flat through Q3.
Beat & raised (Jun 11) yet sold off; AI-moat fear (Claude Design), CFO exit, ARR de-emphasis — the narrative, not the numbers, drives it.
China export-license tightening + Senate scrutiny; the memory/chip complex swings on AI-spending sentiment.
No bad news — strong Q1, IBM AI deal. But it's the biggest weight + a high multiple; in a hawkish-Fed software de-rate it leads the drawdown.
Trump MFN pricing deals (Gilead, Novartis signed) + import tariffs put a pricing-pressure overhang on the whole pharma cluster.
FY EPS guide cut on deal financing + a weak flu season; revenue raised. Defensive — a yellow flag, not a red one.

sectors.note: Amid multiple earnings-related catalysts across the sector including weak Hubspot FY26 sales and Q3 EPS guidance, Datadog Q3 adjusted EPS and sales guidance that was only slightly above estimates, and Applovi's worse-than-expected Q2 sales results.

As risk assets enjoy a tailwind. Also, financial results and commentary from companies such as ON Semiconductor and Palantir may help support the ongoing themes of chip supply shortages and growing demand from an expansionary AI services sector.

sectors.driver: Softer oil prices have driven a decline in Treasury yields
sectors.note: As softer oil prices have driven a decline in Treasury yields, helping ease inflation concerns and support expectations for a more favorable rate environment. The improved macro backdrop has lifted sentiment across the financial sector.

sectors.driver: Reports suggesting that the Iranian government will try to delay a deal …
sectors.note: After reports suggesting that the Iranian government will try to delay a deal with the U.S. An impasse may mean that bottlenecking of feedstock cargoes may continue with limited Strait of Hormuz marine passage.
